Servers only. Turn this on to add the mod to a server world that was started without it: back up the server, turn this on, delete map_basements.bin from the server's save folder, and restart. House basements stay as they were, and the sewers and caves appear wherever nobody has been yet. Players who joined before must delete their own copy of map_basements.bin for this server once; the game tells them where. Leave it off on a server that started with the mod. Single player works this out by itself.

Deep dug tunnels with no shaft near, and the far ends of a cave, have stale air that slowly wears you down; a blast or a burning coal seam fouls the air for hours and makes you sick unless you wear a mask or breathing gear. A canary warns you first. Turn this off and the air below ground is always fresh.
The most rock any single charge can open, however big it is. 64 = a small room. Raise it if you want a TNT barrel to open a chamber.
How likely a square caught in a blast is set alight, at the centre of it, falling off toward the edge. 0 stops a charge starting fires; anything above about 50 will burn out a furnished cellar.
The share of blasted squares that leave their stone, ore or coal on the floor. 1 = every square, as if it had been dug by hand; 0 = the blast leaves nothing to pick up.
Whether dynamite or TNT set below ground opens the rock around it. Off, the charges still bang, hurt and burn like any other bomb, and leave the rock standing.

How fast an oxygen tank and a mask filter are used up, against the game's own rate. 1.0 leaves them exactly as the base game spends them; 0 makes them last for ever; 4 empties them four times as fast. Below ground a running tank also uses Oxygen tank drain below ground.
Caves and mines map shows everything
Off: caves and mines go on the map as you find them, or when you read a survey map. On: every cave and mine, every level, is on the map from the start.

The eight caves under the old dry wells, the well ropes and the cave survey map. Off: the wells are ordinary wishing wells. Decided when the world is made: a world already started keeps the underground it was made with.
The chance, per coal square a blast opens, that the coal catches fire. 0 means blasting a seam never lights it.

How far the light spreads from directly under an open manhole at midday. 6 = current, enough to light the landing and a little of the walkway. Lower it for a narrow beam, raise it to light most of a chamber.

An opened manhole lets the sun down into the room below it. The shaft brightens and fades with the time of day and dims under heavy weather. Turn this off to keep the sun out of the sewer; its own lamps are not affected.
How fast cracks, vines and weeds take hold in the sewer, on top of the game's own Erosion Speed setting. 1 keeps pace with the world above; 0 leaves the tunnels exactly as they were built.
How many of the sewer's dead have mushrooms growing out of them. 0 turns the bloom off entirely.
How green and murky the sewer air reads. It tints the view and drains some of its colour while you are in the sewer, and lifts the moment you climb out. 0 leaves the sewer its own colour.
On: a manhole cover is pried up with a crowbar. Off: it can be lifted by hand.
Off: the Miner is not offered at character creation. A character who already has it keeps it.

The 22 mines under their shaft entrances and the mine survey map. Digging your own tunnels works either way. Decided when the world is made: a world already started keeps the underground it was made with.
Used only when the game's global XP multiplier is switched off, like the game's own per-skill multipliers.
How long a sown mushroom tray takes to fruit while it is kept below ground. Game hours. Bringing a tray up into daylight kills the spawn and the clock starts over.

A character saved with a trait from a removed mod will not load. Turn this on, load every character once and save: this mod's traits and the Miner profession come off each character as it loads. Then the mod can be removed from a single-player game. A multiplayer world that has ever run this mod must keep it: the game will not let players join a server it was removed from.

The most live rats anywhere at once, across every sewer you have opened. 20 = current, 40 = maximum. They come out of holes in the walls, only below ground and never in view, and go back when you walk away; 0 turns them off.
Off: throw a grappling hook and climb, no falls. On: you also need a carabiner, and the game's own rope fall check runs, so a tired, heavily loaded or hurt climber can fall.
How many zombies are sealed into the sewer's side rooms. 0 leaves them empty; 1 is one to three per room.
The Strength level a character needs to throw a grappling hook up a wall. Climbing a rope already hung needs none; Strength and Fitness set how fast anyone climbs.
Leave the game's ladders to SMB Steps

Only matters when SMB Steps is on. The game's own ladders are then climbed SMB Steps' way, and this mod's manhole, catwalk and well ladders and wall ropes stay this mod's. Off: this mod climbs the game's ladders too, and both mods offer to climb them.
How long a bucket of guano soak steeps before it turns to nitre liquor, ready to boil down for saltpeter. Game hours.
Off: the sewer map fills in as you walk the tunnels. On: every tunnel under every town is on the map from the start.

What drinking straight from the sewer channel does. Tainted: the game's own tainted water, a little poison, boil it clean. Deadly at once: light poison, food sickness and sickness the moment you drink. Deadly over hours: the same three, building over four hours. Water carried out in a bottle is tainted either way and boils clean.

The sewer under every town: its manholes, side rooms and crawl tunnels, the sewer view on the map and the sewer works map. Off: every manhole is plain street. Decided when the world is made: a world already started keeps the underground it was made with.
Hours a body in the sewer takes to grow one stage further, from clean through to fully fruiting. 0 freezes every zombie where it is.
How badly the spores affect you underground. It builds near fruiting bodies, a mask cuts most of it, and it clears once you are back in clean air. 0 turns it off.

How many squares of rock one dynamite stick opens. 8 = the eight squares around it. Bigger charges scale from this, but less than in proportion: at 8 a TNT crate opens about 34 and a TNT barrel about 64.

Who can sink a shaft or dig stairs down from the surface. Admins only matters on servers; single player digs as normal. Digging stairs up out of a cave, a sewer or a mine is always allowed, so nobody is ever shut in below ground.

Off: the mod's fifteen mushrooms are found only below ground. On: they also turn up when foraging above ground, wherever and whenever the game's own wild mushrooms do. Takes effect when the world loads.

How fast a switched-on oxygen tank empties while you are below ground, on top of the breathing gear drain rate. The base game empties a full tank in about five and a half minutes at normal speed, in fresh air or foul; 0.25 makes one last about 22 minutes down here, and 1.0 is the base game's rate. Tanks on the surface are left alone.
How bright the sewer reads. 1 is its lamps at full strength; lower darkens the whole view evenly while you are in the sewer, torches included.
Caves keep one temperature all year round, and the sewer runs a few degrees warmer. Single player only: on a server the weather above sets the temperature below ground.
Deep Lungs and Bad Back traits
Off: the two traits are not offered at character creation. A character who already has one keeps it.
A steel drum of acid, and somebody left it down here rather than pay to have it taken away. Deadly to drink and no use to anyone until there is a bench to pour it on.
A flat sheet hammered out at the forge. Fill it with soil and it is a mushroom tray; it comes back when the tray is harvested.
Alive, folded up and deeply unimpressed. It went into the trap after the insects on the bait.
The empty case of a car battery. Fill it with lead plates and acid to make that battery again.
Arm and set it from the inventory menu, then get clear: it goes off on its own a few seconds later. Below ground it breaks the rock around it. On the surface it only bangs and burns.
Arm and set it from the inventory menu, link a remote to it, and trigger it from a distance. Below ground it breaks the rock around it. On the surface it only bangs and burns.
Carry it underground. It goes quiet in stale air and dies in foul air, a few minutes before you would feel it.
It stopped singing, and then it stopped. Whatever it was breathing, so were you.
A climbing clip. With realistic climbing on, you need one to climb a wall on a grappling hook.
A county survey with eight dry wells ringed in red. Each has a cave at the bottom.
A bat off the cave roof, dead a while. There is a colony somewhere above you. A mouthful of meat if you cook it, and a bad idea if you do not.
A digital watch with a depth gauge. Worn on either wrist, it shows the time and how many levels below ground you are.
Purple fluorspar, mined from a cave node. Crush it with a hammer for the flux a zinc smelt needs.
Crushed fluorspar. A zinc smelt takes one.
Heavy grey lead ore, mined from a cave node. Two smelt to a lead ingot at a primitive furnace; four refined at a furnace also give up a little silver.
A steel drum of petrol, stencilled GAS. Heavy enough that moving one is a decision. Draw from it the way you would a jerrycan.
A pale cap that grows on bare cave rock. One kind leaves you dizzy and lighter of heart; its twin looks the same and kills. Someone who knows their mushrooms can tell them apart.
Thrown up a wall, it catches the first edge in reach and holds the rope to climb. Comes back when you take the rope down, a little more worn each time.
Grilled over an open fire. Ready to eat.

Bat droppings from the cave floor. Pick them up with a shovel or a trowel, or in gloves, or they end up on your hands. Soak four in a bucket of water: after a couple of days the water is nitre liquor, which boils down to saltpeter. Or brew them into manure tea for the crops.
Soft white gypsum, mined from a cave node. Heat two at a primitive furnace for raw plaster.
A soft, heavy ingot of lead, smelted from galena.
A cast lead plate. Battery plates are lead on both sides; charging does the rest.
Lowered down a hole one level deep, it stands on the floor below and is climbed like any ladder. Take it back up from either end.
An old mining company map with its claims ringed in red. Dig down inside a ring: iron from five levels under, coal past twelve.
Clips to the mount on a mining helmet and leaves both hands free. Runs off a battery.
Clips to the mount on a mining helmet. Needs a light bulb before it will do anything.
Teaches: Boil Down Nitre Liquor, Make Black Powder.

Teaches: Roast Pyrite, Make Coke from Coal, Smelt Galena, Refine Silver from Galena, Smelt Sphalerite, Make Brass Ingot from Zinc, Calcine Gypsum, Burn Zinc to Zinc Oxide, Cast Brass Doorknobs, Make Battery Acid, Cast Lead Plates, Melt Zinc Scrap.
A length of fallen hardwood. Drill it, plug the holes with spawn and keep it below ground, and it will crop again and again until the fungus has eaten the wood.

Steel shelving for growing mushrooms on, two squares long and built in either direction. Stand trays on it and the rack takes on their look as they come along -- bare, then soil, then spores, then a shelf you can pick. It changes nothing about how they grow; keep it below ground.
Sliced for the pan or the pot. They keep about as long as the mushroom did.
A stump dug out whole, roots and all. Heavy, and worth the carry: set it down somewhere dark below ground and it will grow mushrooms for months.
A tray of soil waiting for spores. Sow it with a spore print, then keep it below ground while the mushrooms grow.
A steel drum of oil. Nothing in the world wants it yet, which is a good reason to hang on to the ones you find.

Reads the air where you stand -- how much oxygen is left in it as a share of open air, where you are, and whether anything else is in it. Carry it and the readout sits beside the clock. It tells you nothing about what is left in your own supply.
Fool's gold, dug out of a coal seam or found on a cave floor. Roast two at a furnace for sulfur and a lump of iron ore.
Loose plaster from burnt gypsum. Bag it in paper or newspaper to store it as plaster powder.
White nitre crystals, boiled down from a bucket of steeped guano or scraped off a cave wall. Three parts of this, one of charcoal and one of sulfur is black powder.
Sliced mushrooms in fat, in the pan. Cook it on a stove or a fire, then eat from the pan.
One town's sewer, drawn up by the public works office. Read it to fill that town in on your sewer map.
Two planks laid across the channel. Anyone can put a board down; it will hold you, and not much more.
Dark resinous zinc ore, mined from a cave node. Smelt two at a furnace with coke and flux for a zinc ingot; zinc and copper make brass.
A cap laid on paper leaves its spores behind. Sow a tray of soil with it and keep the tray below ground.
Yellow brimstone, roasted out of pyrite at a furnace. The third part of black powder.
Ready to pick. Harvesting gives the mushrooms back and leaves the soil for the next sowing.
White threads are spreading through the soil. Keep it below ground: daylight kills the spawn and the clock starts over. Mushrooms in a few days.
Carved from one log so the acid cannot leak. Fill it with lead plates and acid for a car battery.
An ingot of zinc, smelted from sphalerite. One with a copper ingot makes brass at a furnace.
Disinfects a wound or a burn. Five uses. Leaves the jar when used up.
A sealed jar of white powder from burning zinc. Mixed with lard it makes an ointment.
The zinc can of a taken-apart battery. Eight melt into a zinc ingot.
Needs a pickaxe, hammer or stone maul.
The air is foul. You can taste it.
The air down here is stale and heavy.
The blast broke %1 squares of rock.
The charge went off inside a room. Only the walls to break, and dynamite will not take those down.
Nothing on your face and nothing on your back.
There is rock straight above you.
Digging up. Swing at the floor in front to open the rock above it.
Your flame burns low and blue.
There is nothing under this one worth opening.
There is nowhere beside it to slide the grate.
You need a crowbar to get under the edge of it.
Something sharp in the rock cuts your hand.
Bare hands: hold Shift and swing at rock to the north or west to claw stairs up.
By hand you can only claw stairs up into rock to the north or west.
Bare-handed, you can only claw your way up.
Needs a wooden ladder or a grappling hook.
A wooden ladder reaches one level down.
Too deep for a wooden ladder.
The cover has been taken away.
The cover is back on. You will push it off on your way out.
There is a vehicle parked over this manhole.
The boards come off for good and you keep the planks.
Needs a crowbar or a hammer.
Ctrl + swing at the floor: a shaft
Ctrl + Shift + swing: stairs, up to the north or west, down to the south or east
Mining on. Your swings dig now.
Needs a propane torch with 3 uses and a welder mask or welding goggles.
You need two planks and two nails.
Needs a propane torch with 2 uses and a welder mask or welding goggles.
You need a pickaxe to cut into that.
You need a crowbar to lift this.
You need a rope or a sheet rope.
You need an empty sack to carry the dirt.
You need an empty sack to carry the gravel.
You need an empty sack to carry the sand.
You need a shovel or a pickaxe to dig down through earth.
You need a sledgehammer for masonry.
You need a stake, a rope, and a hammer, pickaxe or sledgehammer.
Needs a propane torch and a welder mask.
Needs a propane torch with 2 uses, welding rods with 2 uses and a welder mask or welding goggles.
The net comes up with nothing this time.
You need three clear squares of your own tunnel ahead of you.
There is no ladder to climb here.
Not enough solid ground here for a flight of stairs.
Turns it on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the carried canary beside the clock. Its warnings still show over your head with it hidden.

Turns it on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the depth reading from a worn depth meter.

Turns the environment line on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the red or green line under the clock row that says whether the air where you stand is safe.
Turns it on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the filter gauge from a worn gas mask or respirator.
Turns it on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the O2 levels gauge from a carried oxygen sensor.
Show or hide the oxygen supply
Turns it on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the oxygen supply gauge from a worn air tank.

From your next launch, times how long this mod's code takes and writes it once a minute to HydeCoUnderGround_HandlerTimes.txt in the Lua folder inside your Zomboid folder. Leave it off unless you are checking performance.
Show or hide the mining pickaxe
Turns it on or off. There is no key until you pick one.
Shows the pickaxe beside the clock that lights up while mining mode is on. Mining mode still works with it hidden.
Too big to just put down. Place it instead.
Hooks the grappling hook on the edge and lets the rope down. Take the rope down to get the hook back.
You cannot dig on someone else's safehouse.
Set a mine prop (2 planks, 2 nails)
Digging here would cut into the well shaft.
There is nothing below this square to dig into.
The spores are getting to you
You can taste the spores in the air.
Your throat is raw and you keep coughing.
You are breathing more spore than air.
There is nowhere to step off at the top.
Stairs can only be dug to the north or the west.
There is open space over the steps that is not yours to take out.
There is already open space where the steps would go.
That would cut into somebody else's floor.
You cannot cut steps into the sewer itself.

Knox Underground: your saved basement layout for this server is from before the mod was added, so the sewers and caves won't work for you. Quit, delete map_basements.bin from Zomboid/saves/Multiplayer/%1, and join again.

Knox Underground: this save's basement layout was made without the mod's sewers, caves and mines, so it has no underground. To add it: quit, delete map_basements.bin from Zomboid/Saves/%1, and load the save again. House basements stay as they are; places you have already been stay without the underground.
Only admins can start a mine from the street here.
Mines cannot be started from the street here.
White threads are running through it. Down here in the dark it will fruit in a few days.
Spent straw has to be broken up. You need a shovel, a garden fork or a rake.
Spent straw is compost. You need an empty sack to put it in.
A stump has to be dug out. You need a shovel.
You need %1 spore prints of %2. You have %3.
Nothing will take up out here. Carry it down below ground and sow it there.
You need open ground overhead to sink a shaft here.
Tie a rope to the well
The rope would not tie here.
There is no plain rock above this square to dig into.
The street is right above. Dig stairs up instead.
Throws the grappling hook up to the first edge in reach and climbs the rope. Take the rope down to get the hook back. On the rope, press forward to climb up or back to climb down.
You need a carabiner to climb.
Nothing in reach for the hook to catch on.
There is no wall here to climb.
There is no room above you to throw it.
Realistic climbing: you can fall if you are tired, heavily loaded or hurt.
You are not strong enough to climb a wall on a rope.
This one just ends in dirt.
You worked the seams before the world ended. You start with three levels of Mining, know the powder work and the furnace work, and swing a pick like you mean it.

Less knockback from melee weapons.
Decreased carrying weight.
Every swing of a pick or shovel below ground costs you more breath.
Stale air and foul air below ground wear on you at half the rate.

At home in tight spaces below ground.
Cannot be Claustrophobic.
